record.paper_title: Hadronic production of η–mesons: recent results and open questions
record.original_question: What, if any, is the relationship between the two proposed explanations of the unexpectedly low Roper resonance in the light-baryon spectrum: the picture in which the Roper resonance is dynamically generated and P11(1710) is the first quark state, and the picture in which a flavor-dependent quark-quark interaction changes the ordering of states? A satisfactory answer should also address how the situation changes if chiral dynamics really makes S11(1535) a dynamically generated state, because that would worsen the disagreement between the low-lying baryon spectrum and the original nonrelativistic quark-model ordering.

evidence.quote: To my understanding there are so far two possible explanations of the spectrum in the literature, one, where the Roper is generated dynamically and thus interpreting the P11(1710) as the first quark state [12,13], and another, where the ordering of states was changed by introducing a flavor dependent quark–quark interaction [14].
At present it is not clear what the connection between these two pictures is — if such a connection exits at all.
Recently the whole situation became even more confusing for it was claimed that based on chiral dynamics the S11(1535) appears as a dynamically generated state [15,16].
It is therefore of high importance to understand the nature of the low lying resonances for this promises deep insights into how the nature makes hadrons.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the light-baryon spectrum of QCD, with particular focus on the low-lying nucleon resonances: the Roper resonance N(1440) with quantum numbers P11, the P11(1710), and the negative-parity S11(1535). In the original nonrelativistic constituent quark model, the lowest positive-parity radial excitation of the nucleon is predicted to lie above the lowest negative-parity excitation, in conflict with the observed ordering in which the Roper N(1440) lies below the S11(1535). Two distinct theoretical pictures have been proposed to resolve this discrepancy:

(A) A "dynamically generated" picture in which the Roper N(1440) is not a genuine three-quark state but arises as a meson–baryon quasi-bound state generated by coupled-channel hadronic dynamics, and in which the first genuine radial three-quark excitation of the nucleon is identified instead with P11(1710).

(B) A "modified quark–quark interaction" picture in which the Roper N(1440) remains a genuine three-quark state, but a flavor-dependent (e.g. Goldstone-boson-exchange-type) quark–quark interaction is introduced into the constituent quark model so as to reorder the radial and orbital excitations and place the P11 nucleon excitation below the S11.

Determine whether there is a precise mathematical/dynamical relationship between pictures (A) and (B): for instance, whether one can be derived as an effective limit or rearrangement of the other, whether they make distinguishable predictions for observables (such as electromagnetic transition form factors, decay couplings, or large-N_c scaling), or whether they are genuinely inequivalent descriptions of the same spectrum. In the analysis, address also the scenario in which chiral coupled-channel dynamics generates S11(1535) itself as a dynamically generated (e.g. KΣ–ηN) state, and explain how each picture must be modified to accommodate this, including the assignment of the lowest genuine three-quark negative-parity nucleon excitation in that case.
artifact.status_search_result: The nature of the Roper resonance — genuine three-quark state versus dynamically generated meson–baryon structure — and its relation to flavor-dependent quark-interaction models and to a possibly dynamically generated S11(1535) remains an active debate. Recent lattice QCD, Dyson–Schwinger/Faddeev, and coupled-channel studies (e.g. 2017–2026) give differing answers, and a survey from 2026 explicitly describes the Roper as "still controversial 60 years later." No unified reconciliation of the two pictures has been established.

status_evidence.title: The Roper Resonance: Still Controversial 60 Years Later
status_evidence.snippet: Survey emphasizing that the nature of the Roper resonance remains controversial and actively debated.
status_evidence.claim: The dispute between genuine quark-state and dynamically generated interpretations of the Roper is still unresolved.

status_evidence.title: The Roper resonance: a genuine quark state or a dynamically generated structure?
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses the competing interpretations of the Roper resonance and the coupled-channel mechanism producing a quasi-bound state near 1.4 GeV.
status_evidence.claim: Both pictures continue to be pursued in the literature without a consensus reconciliation.

status_evidence.title: The Roper resonance and kin
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2025) review covering Roper-like states and including dynamically generated interpretations of S11(1535).
status_evidence.claim: S11(1535) is frequently treated as a dominantly dynamically generated meson-baryon state, complicating the spectrum interpretation.
